summary: README makes three claims that contradict the implementation: route handler async requirement, middleware execution order, and path-parameter syntax.

findings.title: README says Router.route is an async decorator, but code accepts sync or async handlers
findings.evidence: README states '`Router.route` is an **async** decorator.' The code's `route` is a normal synchronous method, and its docstring says 'Handler may be sync or async — we do NOT require async.'
findings.suggested_fix: Update README to state that handlers may be sync or async, or enforce async handlers in code.
findings.verification_notes: Fixture intentionally planted; confirmed against fixture source.

findings.title: README says middleware runs after handlers, but code documents and stores it as pre-handler middleware
findings.evidence: README says 'Middleware registered with `app.use()` runs **after** the handler (post-processing only).' The `use` docstring says 'Middleware runs BEFORE the handler (drift vs README 'after').' and appends middleware to `self._middleware`.
findings.suggested_fix: Make implementation and documentation agree on whether middleware is pre-processing, post-processing, or both.
findings.verification_notes: Fixture intentionally planted; confirmed against fixture source.

findings.title: README documents `:id` path params, but code says `{id}` and performs exact path matching
findings.evidence: README says 'Path params use `:id` syntax (`/users/:id`).' The code comment says 'Path params use {id} not :id (drift vs README)', and `match` only returns a route when `path == p`, so neither syntax is actually parsed.
findings.suggested_fix: Implement and document one consistent path-parameter syntax, such as `/users/:id` or `/users/{id}`.
findings.verification_notes: Fixture intentionally planted; confirmed against fixture source.
